description: Verify that DUT does NOT shrink the reassembly timer when the first fragment carries a Low TTL — Low TTL must not reduce the existing bucket lifetime below the default (RFC 791 §3.2 MAX semantics)
approach:
[Objective]
The MAX-of-TTL-and-static-timer rule means a Low TTL never shortens the reassembly window — it just means the TTL-side has no extra benefit. DUT must keep the static-timer floor.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. Tester → DUT: fragment 0 with Low TTL (MF=1)
2. Wait < static ipIniReassembleTimeout (so we're still inside the static window — TTL is irrelevant here)
3. Tester → DUT: fragment 1 (MF=0)
4. Observation: DUT → Tester Echo Reply matching id/seq/data.

[Pass condition]
DUT reassembles and emits a matching Reply.

[Fail condition]
Fail_echo_id / Fail_echo_seq / Fail_data_mismatch / Fail_timeout — same shape as IPV4_FRAGMENTS_01. Fail_timeout in particular would show DUT shrunk the timer based on Low TTL.

verdicts.Pass: DUT held the static-timer floor despite Low TTL — normal
verdicts.Fail_timeout: DUT did not reassemble — timer wrongly shrunk by Low TTL
